title: Black Bear Buys Thriller ‘Seeker,’ Starring ‘Obsession’s’ Cooper Tomlinson and ‘Off Campus’ Actor Mika Abdalla (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Black Bear has acquired “Seeker,” a thriller featuring “Obsession” actor Cooper Tomlinson, “Off Campus” breakout Mika Abdalla and “Happy Death Day”
body:
Black Bear has acquired “Seeker,” a thriller featuring “Obsession” actor Cooper Tomlinson, “Off Campus” breakout Mika Abdalla and “Happy Death Day” star Jessica Rothe.

	The company has North American and U.K. distribution rights to the movie, which was introduced to buyers at this year’s AFM. Directed by Adam Carter Rehmeier and written by Michael Learner, “Seeker” follows Grant (Tomlinson), whose fiancée Caroline (Abdalla) mysteriously disappeared five years earlier. Now a ride-share driver, his life is upended when he picks up a passenger who he is convinced is responsible for her absence. As the logline teases, “What starts as a tense game of cat-and-mouse spirals into something far stranger, more disturbing, and deeply unhinged — challenging everything we think we know.”
	

	“’Seeker’ is exactly the type of bold and propulsive storytelling we look for at Black Bear,” said Katie Anderson, Black Bear’s executive VP of acquisitions. “Michael’s script had us all on the edge of our seats, and with Adam’s singular voice and this cast’s incredible talent, we couldn’t be more excited to bring this film to theaters.”

	Alex Lebovici and Learner will produce for Hammerstone Studios, with Adam McKay and Todd Schulman for HyperObject Industries, and Noah Centineo and Enzo Marc of Arkhum Productions. Samuel Hall and Warren Goz will executive-produce for North Five Six, alongside Ibrahim Mohammed, Yasmyne Mohammed, Chase Vergari, Karina Manashil, David Goldman and Andria Spring.

	“Seeker” will begin production in January in Washington. The film is fully financed by Hammerstone Studios and Script 2 Screen. North Five Six are representing international distribution rights, with CAA Media Finance having represented U.S. rights.
	

	Black Bear was founded in 2011 as independent production studio and recently launched a domestic distribution arm. The company’s latest theatrical release, the offbeat romantic dramedy “Wicker,” has been a box office winner with $40 million globally to date. Black Bear’s upcoming slate includes Guy Ritchie’s “Wife & Dog,” starring Benedict Cumberbatch and Rosamund Pike; and David Leitch’s “Jason Statham Stole My Bike” led by Statham and Hannah Waddingham. It also recently nabbed Bill Hader’s feature directing debut, “They Know,” a psychological horror film starring Hader and Linda Cardellini.

title: Patrick Stewart Was ‘Struggling’ on Last Day of Filming ‘Avengers: Doomsday’; Marvel Plans to Add Tribute to Movie
description: Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and co-directors Anthony and Joe Russo are getting candid about filming “Avengers: Doomsday” with the late sta
body:
Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and co-directors Anthony and Joe Russo are getting candid about filming “Avengers: Doomsday” with the late star Patrick Stewart, whose role became his final on-screen appearance after his death in October.

	“He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew,” Feige told Entertainment Weekly of Stewart’s final day shooting. “We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.”
	

	In “Avengers: Doomsday,” Stewart reprises his “X-Men” character Charles Xavier for the ninth and final time; even before his passing, EW notes that Stewart was offered a role in the film’s sequel, “Avengers: Secret Wars,” due out in Dec. 2027, but declined. “It was in the back of all of our heads, we may never see him on set again,” Anthony said, describing the atmosphere as “very emotional.”

	Anthony continued: “It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew. You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”
	

	Stewart died after a brief battle with Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia on Oct. 29, and both Feige and the Russo brothers are currently planning how best to pay tribute to the actor in the forthcoming film. “We’re long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us,” he said. “We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.”

	“In a lot of ways, Xavier’s the conscience in the movie,” said Joe. “He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who’s his best friend, in the film. It’s a very emotional scene about forgiveness, and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing.”

	“Avengers: Doomsday” hits theaters on Dec. 18.

title: Curry Barker’s ‘Anything But Ghosts’ to Release in Premium HDR by Barco – Film News in Brief
description: “Obsession” director Curry Barker is returning with his second feature film, “Anything But Ghosts,” which will be released in premium HDR by Barco.
body:
“Obsession” director Curry Barker is returning with his second feature film, “Anything But Ghosts,” which will be released in premium HDR by Barco.

	The film, which follows a group of fame-seeking aspiring “ghosthunters” navigating terrifyingly unfamiliar territory, premieres in theaters May 7 and features a cast including Violet McGraw, Chris Reinacher, Bryce Dallas Howard and Aaron Paul.


	“Anything But Ghosts” is written and directed by Barker and co-written by Cooper Tomlinson, with the duo also starring in the film. Roy Lee, Steven Schneider, Jason Blum, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath produce.
	
	
		Monday, Nov. 23	

	Randy Newman to Receive Society of Composers & Lyricists Lifetime Achievement Award

	Randy Newman, the composer and songwriter behind Disney classics including “Toy Story,” “Cars” and “Monsters, Inc.,” will be honored by the Society of Composers & Lyricists with the Lifetime Achievement Award on Dec. 9 at the 37th Annual SCL Holiday Dinner in Los Angeles.

	Newman has received many honors over his decades-spanning career, including seven Grammys, three Emmys and two Academy Awards, as well as a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. He was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2002 and the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2013.

	In addition to Newman’s honor, the society will posthumously induct Marvin Hamlisch and Earle Hagen into its Hall of Fame at the event.

	Hamlisch was the composer of more than 40 motion picture scores, including his Oscar-winning score and song for “The Way We Were” and “The Sting.” He has received Pulitzer, Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony Awards.
	

	Hagen’s credits included “The Dick Van Dyke Show,” “The Danny Thomas Show,” “That Girl,” “The Mod Squad,” “Planet of the Apes” and “Eight Is Enough,” among many others. The Emmy-winning and Oscar-nominated composer was inducted into the Television Academy Hall of Fame in 2011.

	Other honorees include Jon Batiste, who will receive the Ambassador Award in New York on Dec. 1; Brent McCorkle, who will receive the Trailblazer Award in Nashville on Dec. 5; and Sen. Dick Durbin (D-IL), who will receive the Excellence in Advocacy Award in Chicago on Dec. 3.

title: Philip Rosenberg, Oscar-Winning Production Designer for ‘All That Jazz,’ Dies at 91
description: Philip Rosenberg, a production designer and art director who was part of the team that won the art direction-set decoration Oscar for “All That Jaz
body:
Philip Rosenberg, a production designer and art director who was part of the team that won the art direction-set decoration Oscar for “All That Jazz,” died Oct. 28 in West Palm Beach, Florida. He was 91. 

	His death was announced by his nephew, Alan Rosenberg. 

	Rosenberg’s first film job was as design assistant on the 1968 “The Sea Gull.” He went on to become an art director and production designer, working with New York-based directors such as Sidney Lumet, Paul Mazursky and Norman Jewison. He partnered with production designer Tony Walton on films including “The Wiz” and “All That Jazz.” 
	

	Known for being part of the realist school of production design in the 1970s, he was nominated for an Oscar as art director of “The Wiz.” Among his other credits were “The Owl and the Pussycat,” “Next Stop Greenwich Village,” “The Gambler,” “Network,” “The Sentinel,” “Running on Empty,” “Night Falls on Manhattan” and “Moonstruck.” His final credit came for “Collateral Damage” in 2002.

	Rosenberg grew up in Prospect Park South, Flatbush, Brooklyn, and studied scenic design at Yale. After graduation, he was hired as an assistant at the Metropolitan Opera, as well as assisting Marcel Vertès on the murals in the Cafe Carlyle. 

	He married Siv Sandstrom, a hostess in the Swedish pavilion at the 1964 World’s Fair, who assisted him in the art department on films including “Running on Empty” and “Moonstruck.” She died in 2024. 

	He is survived by his brothers Stanley Rosenberg and David Rosenberg and six nieces and nephews.

title: Indonesia-France Film Lab Unveils Six Projects as Paris Readies First Southeast Asia Co-Production Forum (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Six Indonesian projects, each from a director-producer pairing working on a debut or sophomore feature, have been chosen for the 2026 Indonesia-Fra
body:
Six Indonesian projects, each from a director-producer pairing working on a debut or sophomore feature, have been chosen for the 2026 Indonesia-France Film Lab X MTN Lab, which runs Nov. 25-30 in Yogyakarta as part of JAFF Market.

	Now in its third edition, the lab is run by the French Embassy and the Institut français d’Indonésie (IFI), with French film school La Fémis supplying the mentors. Indonesian partners include the Ministry of Culture’s Directorate of Film, Music and Arts, through its national talent management program, MTN, as well as the Indonesia Film Agency (BPI) and the Association of Indonesian Film Producers (Aprofi). The long-term aim is to seed French-Indonesian co-productions.
	

	“Indonesian filmmakers have never lacked stories. What they have lacked is structured access to international partners,” said Fauzan Zidni, chairman of BPI. “BPI is committed to working with the Ministry of Culture, the French Embassy, CNC and our industry associations to make sure these projects get made.”

	French script consultant Eric Collins leads the story development strand, working with each team individually to sharpen each project’s artistic vision and international prospects. A separate two-day industry workshop covers development, financing, international distribution and the workings of the French film business. It is led by producers Vincent Wang of House On Fire and Thibaut Amri of Avant La Nuit, along with Sébastien Chesneau of sales company Cercamon.

	The selection comprises “A Straight Way to Love,” written and directed by Kurnia Alexander and produced by Eliza Cheisa; “An Interesting Incident,” directed by Rizal Hanun, who co-wrote it with producer Janice Angelica; “Father Figure,” from writer-director Rizaldy Bagas and producer Mo Amputra; “My Tears, a Sea for Jakarta to Sink,” written and directed by Andrea Nirmala Widjajanto and produced by Nirartha Bas Diwangkara; “Saltstorm!,” from writer-director Al Ridwan and producer Utari Hanif Assyuri; and “Super Neli,” co-directed by Robby Ul Pratama, who also produces, and Anggi Frisca from a script by Resty Savira Oktaviani and Sally Anom Sari.
	

	“It is particularly fascinating to discover how strongly traditional culture resonates in contemporary Indonesian storytelling,” said Julie Tingaud, deputy head of international affairs at La Fémis.

	Teams from last year’s edition get their next shot in December. The inaugural Southeast Asia Film Forum takes place in Paris Dec. 9-13, hosted by France’s CNC, the Centre Pompidou and the French cultural network. Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines are the four partner nations, and the program mixes panels, screenings and an institutional strand around a central slate of co-production meetings.

	Indonesia’s presence will be backed by the Ministry of Culture’s film directorate. BPI will take part in the institutional program, filmmaker Edwin will present two of his films, and the 2025 lab teams will pitch to French producers.

	Fabien Penone, France’s ambassador to Indonesia, Timor-Leste and ASEAN, said the lab built on the joint cultural strategy adopted by French President Emmanuel Macron and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto at Borobudur on May 29, 2025, and that last year’s duos would arrive in Paris after a year of mentoring from La Fémis. “This is precisely our ambition: to turn the growing ties between our two film industries into concrete and long-term collaborations and, ultimately, more co-productions between France and Indonesia,” Penone said.

	The Borobudur declaration calls for a closer, more formal audiovisual alliance between the two countries, with co-production as its centerpiece. The Yogyakarta lab is one of the ways the two countries are building it.

	The JAFF Market runs alongside the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival.

title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35 Finale: Who’s Taking Home the Mirrorball? — Updating Live
description: Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars” is officially coming to an end. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, the five remaining celebrities — Tatyana Ali, Ezra Frech
body:
Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars” is officially coming to an end. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, the five remaining celebrities — Tatyana Ali, Ezra Frech, Amber Glenn, Maura Higgins and Connor Wood — compete one last time for the mirrorball trophy. Each finalist will perform three routines: the instant dance, a freestyle, and judges’ choice.

	Variety will be updating this story live, so keep refreshing through the night for updates.


	Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik (82/90)For judges’ choice, the duo kicked off the night with a sexy salsa to “Jamaican (Bam Bam),” directed by Carrie Ann Inaba, scoring a 27/30. When it came time for the instant dance, the duo drew the jive card, even though she preferred the foxtrot. Carrie Ann called the impressive routine “beyond insane,” and they earned a 27/30. They ended the night with a powerful freestyle to a mashup of Cab Calloway’s “Minnie the Moocher” and Judy Garland’s “Over the Rainbow.” Jan also may have forgotten he was on live TV, blurting out, “I’m so fucking proud” after the routine. They scored a 28, bringing their total to 82.
	

	Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov (90/90)The pair’s judges’ choice dance, with direction from Derek Hough, was a quickstep to “Sing, Sing, Sing,” and they scored the first perfect score of 30 of the night. For the instant dance, they were given a cha cha, dancing to Sabrina Carpenter’s “Tears.” They scored another perfect 30 after leaving Derek speechless. Their Madonna-inspired freestyle to “Like a Prayer” and “Music” was super emotional, with Amber crying midway through. She was also joined by Team USA’s Madison Chock and Evan Bates on the dance floor. Afterward, Derek said, “The queen of the ice is now queen of the ballroom.” The pair earned a perfect 30.
	

	Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold (53/60)Carrie Ann suggested the Viennese waltz for the judges’ choice dance, and they danced to Noah Kahan’s “Willing and Able.” The emotional number earned the pair a 28/30. For the instant dance, they were given a cha cha to The Pussycat Dolls’ “Buttons” — their third cha cha of the season. Carrie Ann called it their best cha cha so far, despite a small mistake. They scored a 25/30.

	Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas (60/60)Assigned a tango by Bruno Tonioli, Team Tink danced to “Gallo Ciego” by Orquesta Color Tango, scoring the second perfect score of 30. For the instant dance, the pair were scared after choosing a quickstep and being assigned Little Richard’s “Tutti Frutti” — a song Maura had never heard of. Bruno complimented her “gorgeously spot on” footwork and Julianne Hough joked Mark had never looked happier than he did after the routine, which earned them a perfect 30.


	Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach (60/60)Going last in the judges’ choice dances, Bruno assigned Ezra and Daniella a steamy salsa to  “Danza Kuduro” by Bruno; their routine earned a perfect score. For the instant dance, they were assigned the tango to Avicii’s “Levels.” Derek thanked Ezra for educating the audience to show what’s possible and complimented his “top-notch” artistry. The pair earned another perfect score.

title: ‘One Last Order’: Beloved Drive-Thru Worker Sighle Williams Says ‘I Miss the Community’ as Viral Netflix Doc Streams
description: Sighle Williams served customers at a Florida burger joint for 37 years. And on her last day at Mac’s Drive Thru, it seemed like the entire city of
body:
Sighle Williams served customers at a Florida burger joint for 37 years. And on her last day at Mac’s Drive Thru, it seemed like the entire city of Gainesville came out to say goodbye.

	“A lot of people told me they were going to come. But I wasn’t expecting that many people,” Williams tells Variety. Mac’s had a three-hour line of cars during her final shift. The restaurant was so busy they actually ran out of burgers. “Some of the people that showed up that day didn’t even know me,” she says. “It’s a good feeling that I made a difference in a lot of people’s lives.”
	

	Williams is the subject of “One Last Order,” a 20-minute documentary that hit Netflix on Tuesday. The film, co-directed by the restaurant owner’s daughter, follows Williams as she hugs emotional customers and recounts spending half her life behind the drive-thru window.

	Williams says the cameras didn’t faze her, but she got emotional during “a moment when I sat in my car and realized it was my last day of work, and how all the people came out to see me off. It was awesome.”

	“It was overwhelming as well,” Williams adds. “I was so hyped up, I didn’t eat all day. I didn’t even go to the restroom.”



	

									COURTESY OF NETFLIX
	



	Mac’s made three times its normal sales on Williams’ last day. As a retirement gift, the owners gave her every dollar that passed through the fast-food window. Between the day’s earnings and generous tips, Williams made nearly an entire year’s salary in a single day, according to the documentary. Williams tells Variety the gift has allowed her to “catch up on some things and save for a rainy day.”
	

	Since retiring, Williams has been back at Mac’s a handful of times — mostly to catch up with her friends. “I miss working, yes, but I also miss the community,” she says. “I miss the customers. That is what I mainly miss.”

	Williams became a beloved fixture in Gainesville for her sunny demeanor and her unique ability to memorize repeat customers’ orders. One customer in the documentary says seeing Williams in the drive-thru window is “like seeing a rainbow every day.”

	“Everybody has their own things going on in their life, and sometimes you just have to take a moment to say, ‘Hey, how are you doing?’ They could be having a rough day, and it made a difference,” Williams says. “Sometimes you have a car full of kids and the mama trying to get the order right. Some people come and they don’t really know what they want. You just have to be patient. People appreciate that.”



	

									COURTESY OF NETFLIX
	



	Williams worked for 37 years while raising five girls on her own. When her sister struggled with drug addiction, she stepped up to parent her two daughters. And a few years later, she took in her niece’s three kids.

	Asked how she remained so cheerful despite difficult circumstances, Williams says, “I’m just a positive person, I guess. They had to go to school. I had to go to work. I had to make sure we had the lights on, doctor’s appointments and everything. I can’t explain it.”

	When Netflix posted the trailer for the film in early November, it went viral on X, gaining more than 11 million views. Williams, who has accompanied the documentary at seven or eight festivals, says she felt like a celebrity before the film even premiered. The week it launched on Netflix, Williams appeared on “CBS Mornings” and “The Jennifer Hudson Show.”

	“I’ve been practicing for the Spirit Tunnel,” she says of the talk show’s viral entrance videos. “I can dance a little bit. I’m going to be cool with it and rock with it.”

title: Oscars Visual Effects Top 20 Revealed: Disney Leads With Four Titles as ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘Ramayana,’ ‘Dune: Part Three’ and ‘Wildwood’ Make the Cut (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The Oscar race for visual effects is down to 20, and the road to the 99th Academy Awards runs through Ithaca, Motunui and a galaxy far, far away.
body:
The Oscar race for visual effects is down to 20, and the road to the 99th Academy Awards runs through Ithaca, Motunui and a galaxy far, far away.

	The Academy’s Visual Effects Branch notified the artisans behind the 20 films advancing to the next round ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Through multiple sources, Variety has confirmed all 20 of the finalists, including Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three,” Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s “Project Hail Mary,” Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day” and Marvel Studios’ “Avengers: Doomsday” from Anthony and Joe Russo.
	

	The Academy does not release the top 20 externally and declines to comment or confirm which films advanced.

	Disney leads the confirmed titles with four. Alongside “Avengers: Doomsday,” the studio lands Jon Favreau’s “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” 20th Century Studios’ “Whalefall” and Thomas Kail’s live-action “Moana,” which brings Dwayne Johnson back as the demigod Maui.

	Skydance (formerly Warner Bros. Discovery) took three of the spots: “Dune: Part Three,” Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s Tom Cruise-led “Digger” and Craig Gillespie’s “Supergirl” from former DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran. But the studio also sees four contenders fall short.

	Villeneuve’s stakes are historic. Both “Dune” and “Dune: Part Two” won the visual effects Oscar, and in March, “Avatar: Fire and Ash” made James Cameron’s franchise three-for-three in the category. “Dune: Part Three,” which opens Dec. 18, now puts Villeneuve two steps from the same trilogy sweep.
	

	Universal Pictures booked both of its summer event films, “The Odyssey” and “Disclosure Day,” while Amazon MGM Studios goes two-for-two with “Project Hail Mary” and Kyle Balda’s “The Sheep Detectives.”

	Nolan’s track record in the category is just as formidable. “Inception,” “Interstellar” and “Tenet” each won the visual effects Oscar. However, the branch famously left “Oppenheimer” off its top 20 for the 96th Academy Awards. Spielberg has been here before, too, with “Jurassic Park,” which won the category in 1994.



	

									Courtesy of Laika
	



	Two of the more intriguing finalists come from outside the Hollywood studio system. Takashi Yamazaki’s “Godzilla Minus Zero” follows “Godzilla Minus One,” which won the category at the 96th Oscars and delivered the franchise its first Academy Award. Laika’s stop-motion “Wildwood,” directed by Travis Knight, gives the studio a chance to return to a category it cracked with Knight’s “Kubo and the Two Strings,” one of only two animated films ever nominated for visual effects, along with “The Nightmare Before Christmas.”

	Sony lands three big movies in the field. Leading the charge is Destin Daniel Cretton’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and the still-to-be-released “Jumanji: Open World,” advancing alongside “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” the Indian mythological epic. “Ramayana” follows S.S. Rajamouli’s “RRR,” which reached the top 20 for the 95th Oscars and signals the branch’s continued appetite for large-scale spectacle from outside Hollywood.

	A24 also lands a spot with “Backrooms,” the feature directorial debut of 21-year-old Kane Parsons, whose YouTube series turned the internet’s liminal-space legend into a box office phenomenon, grossing more than $400 million worldwide.

	Paramount received a split verdict. David Ayer’s survival thriller “Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt, advanced, but Variety confirmed that two of the studio’s other contenders, “Ebenezer” with Johnny Depp and the video game adaptation “Street Fighter,” did not make the top 20.

	Netflix also breaks through with Peter Berg’s epic war drama “The Mosquito Bowl,” one year after the streamer placed “Frankenstein” and “The Electric State” on the shortlist.
	

	Lionsgate gets a spot for themselves with Francis Lawrence’s box office smash prequel “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

	The preliminary voting period for the Oscars shortlist begins Monday, Dec. 7, at 9 a.m. PT and ends Friday, Dec. 11, at 5 p.m. PT. The shortlists in all categories will be announced Tuesday, Dec. 15. Afterward, the VFX bake-offs will take place during the Academy’s Jan. 8-10 voting events, when the 10 shortlisted films will be presented to branch members for final nomination consideration. Nominations voting runs Jan. 11-15, with the nominations announced Thursday, Jan. 21.

	The 99th Academy Awards will be held Sunday, March 14, at the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood and will air live on ABC.

									Â© 2026 Netflix, Inc.
	
					


							
		

	Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.

	Golden Globes Predictions Commentary (Updated: Nov. 24, 2026): Golden Globe voting is underway! Here’s the breakdown of all the submissions.

	Eighty-eight films were submitted for best motion picture (drama), and 43 are competing for best motion picture (musical or comedy). Among the drama submissions are Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” and Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three.” The musical or comedy field also includes Destin Daniel Cretton’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”

	In the lead acting races, the drama category for best actor has 69 submissions representing 64 performers with Brad Pitt in contention for “Heart of the Beast,” alongside Robert Pattinson for “Primetime.” The musical or comedy category features 32 submissions from 31 performers, including Tom Holland for “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and Ryan Gosling for “Project Hail Mary.”

	The best actress (drama) race has 39 submissions from 39 performers, with Zendaya (“Dune: Part Three”) and Anne Hathaway (“Verity”) among the contenders. The musical or comedy field has 23 submissions from 22 performers. Meryl Streep returns as Miranda Priestly in “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” while Olivia Wilde earns two entries, for “I Want Your Sex” and “The Invite.”

	The acting races are led by the supporting actor category, which boasts 221 submissions from 198 performers, making it the most crowded of the six acting fields. Mark Ruffalo has three entries in the supporting category alone: “Being Heumann,” “Crime 101,” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” The supporting actress category has 158 submissions from 146 performers. Florence Pugh appears twice, for “Dune: Part Three” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” while Zendaya is also a double entrant, with submissions for “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” that go along with her two leading bids.

	Behind the camera, 131 filmmakers are attached to 123 films in the best director race, including Steven Spielberg for “Disclosure Day” and Nolan for “The Odyssey.” The screenplay category features 121 submissions, among them Quentin Tarantino’s script for “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” and Drew Goddard’s adaptation of “Project Hail Mary.”

	The music categories include 100 submissions for best original score, with John Williams (“Disclosure Day”) and Hans Zimmer (“Dune: Part Three”) among the composers in contention. Best original song has 51 entries, including Taylor Swift and Jack Antonoff’s “I Knew It, I Knew You” from “Toy Story 5,” as well as two submissions from Diane Warren.

title: Golden Globes: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Goes Comedy, ‘Dune 3’ Skips Box Office Achievement Category and More (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
The Golden Globes ballots are out, and some of the year’s biggest surprises are emerging from the official reminder lists sent to members.

	Variet
body:
The Golden Globes ballots are out, and some of the year’s biggest surprises are emerging from the official reminder lists sent to members.

	Variety has exclusively obtained the official motion picture eligibility list for the 84th Golden Globes, which lays out every film submitted across seven categories along with the actors, directors, writers and composers each studio put forward. The document includes 88 titles for best motion picture (drama), 43 for best motion picture (musical or comedy), 24 animated features, 42 non-English-language films, 100 original scores, 51 original songs and 20 contenders for cinematic and box office achievement.
	

	It reveals some unexpected genre placements, ambitious campaign decisions and performers who could find themselves competing against their own work.

	There’s the musical or comedy race, which Sony has turned into its own blockbuster lane. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which has grossed more than $2 billion worldwide, files on the comedy side of the house with Tom Holland in lead actor. The rest of the ensemble, including Zendaya, Florence Pugh, Mark Ruffalo, Sadie Sink, Marisa Tomei, Jon Bernthal and Tramell Tillman, goes supporting. The studio’s “Jumanji: Open World” follows it in, with Dwayne Johnson, Jack Black and Kevin Hart in lead actor and Karen Gillan in lead actress.

	Netflix’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,” directed by David Fincher from a Quentin Tarantino script, joins both the comedy race and the cinematic and box office achievement race, with Brad Pitt in lead actor.
	

	The cinematic and box office achievement category has 20 entries. Introduced in 2024, it recognizes films that have grossed $150 million, with at least $100 million grossed in the U.S., or have garnered “commensurate digital streaming viewership recognized by trusted industry sources.”

	One notable omission is Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming sci-fi epic “Dune: Part Three,” which appears in Best Motion Picture (Drama) and Best Original Score but not in the box office race. Of course, its actors, including Timothée Chalamet, are in the mix for acting recognition. Even though the Warner Bros. epic is allowed, based on Globes rules, to use projected grosses, it’s opted out of the category, the same as its predecessor, “Dune: Part Two,” which didn’t submit in the category last time around. “Dune: Part Three” opens Dec. 18. For Netflix, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” starts a two-week, IMAX-only run Wednesday before it streams Dec. 23, and it’s already on the box office list.

	The rest of the box office field includes “Backrooms,” “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” “Disclosure Day,” “Focker In-Law,” “GOAT,” “Godzilla Minus Zero,” “Hoppers,” “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” “Jumanji: Open World,” “Michael,” “Minions & Monsters,” “Moana,” “Obsession,” “The Odyssey,” “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie,” “Toy Story 5” and A24’s documentary “You Can See Everything,” the only place it can compete on the ballot, likely making it the frontrunner to win the prize.

	Animation isn’t just found at the kids’ table anymore.

	Eight of the 24 animated submissions also turn up in a best picture category. Netflix’s “Ray Gunn,” from two-time Oscar winner Brad Bird, makes a surprise entry in the drama field alongside Leah Nelson’s “Tangles,” Laika’s “Wildwood” from director Travis Knight and Sony Pictures Classics’ “Iron Boy,” which doubles as a French entry in the non-English language field.

	The musical or comedy side gets its own animated contingent with DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island,” Illumination’s “Minions & Monsters” and “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.” One conspicuous no-show is Pixar’s “Toy Story 5.” The billion-dollar sequel seemed to have skipped the best motion picture (musical or comedy) entirely, competing in animated feature and cinematic and box-office achievement, in addition to Randy Newman’s score and Taylor Swift’s original song “I Knew It, I Knew You.” Interestingly, “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island,” a Japanese dark fantasy from Toho and director Kei Oikawa, makes the opposite call, appearing in non-English language, score and song but not in animated feature at all.
	



	

					Zendaya in “Dune Part Three”
									Warner Bros.
	



	Several performers will be competing against themselves, and a few could do it in two genres at once.Zendaya has four titles in the running. “Dune: Part Three” and “The Drama” put her in both lead actress races, drama and comedy and “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” put her in supporting.Robert Pattinson also has four, with “Primetime” in drama and “The Drama” in comedy for lead actor, plus “Dune: Part Three” and “The Odyssey” in supporting.

	Sandra Hüller makes it a three-way tie at four, with “Rose” in lead actress and “Fatherland,” “Digger” and “Project Hail Mary” in supporting. Anne Hathaway has three: “Verity” in lead actress (drama), “The Devil Wears Prada 2” in lead actress (musical or comedy) and “The Odyssey” in supporting.

	Penélope Cruz has three, with “Bunker” in lead actress and “La Bola Negra” and “The Invite” in supporting. Olivia Wilde has three performances, including “I Want Your Sex” and “The Invite” in lead actress (musical or comedy) and “Behemoth!” in supporting. She is also in the running for one of the six slots for best director for “The Invite.”

	Brad Pitt is in lead actor twice, for “Heart of the Beast” in drama and “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” in musical or comedy. Andrew Garfield has two, with “The Uprising” in lead actor (drama) and “Artificial” in supporting. In addition, Javier Bardem, Mark Ruffalo, Stephen Graham, Willem Dafoe and Caitríona Balfe each have three titles on the list.

	There are 131 directors on the reminder list, 23 of whom are women, or about 18%. They represent a range of categories: drama, including Emerald Fennell (“Wuthering Heights”), Siân Heder (“Being Heumann”), Kelly O’Sullivan (“Mouse,” co-directed with Alex Thompson), Beth de Araújo (“Josephine”), Georgia Oakley (“Sense and Sensibility”), Jennifer Peedom (“Tenzing”), Rachel Morrison (“Love of Your Life”) and Aleshea Harris (“Is God Is”); comedy, including Olivia Wilde (“The Invite”), Jane Schoenbrun (“Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma”), Hayley Kiyoko (“Girls Like Girls”), Alicia MacDonald (“Finding Emily”) and Eleanor Wilson (“Wicker,” co-directed with Alex Huston Fischer); non-English language, including Ildikó Enyedi (“Silent Friend”), Marie Kreutzer (“Gentle Monster”), May el-Toukhy (“Woman Unknown”), Marine Atlan (“La Gradiva”), Myrsini Aristidou (“Hold Onto Me”) and Sandra Wollner (“Everytime”); and animation, including Leah Nelson (“Tangles”), Fawn Veerasunthorn (“Hexed,” co-directed with Jason Hand), Alyce Tzue (“Steps,” co-directed with John Ripa) and Phuong Mai Nguyen (“In Waves”).
	

	Ballots are due Dec. 4. Nominations will be announced Dec. 7, and Nikki Glaser hosts the ceremony Jan. 10 from the Beverly Hilton on CBS and Paramount+.

              Kamala Harris may have her eyes on the White House again ... but for now, she's got her sights set on some high fashion in Paris.
      
    
              The former vice president and her husband, Doug Emhoff, were spotted at a Chanel boutique over the weekend ... taking a little retail therapy break before the 2028 presidential race starts heating up.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Photos obtained by TMZ show Harris and Emhoff relaxing on a couch inside the luxury store, surrounded by designer clothing and several people who appear to be assisting them. There's snacks and glasses of Champagne in front of them, too.
      

              No word on whether she walked away with any pricey purchases ... but she certainly looked right at home.
      
    
              The fashionable outing comes as Harris keeps the door open on another presidential run ... saying she's considering another shot at the White House in 2028 after losing to Donald Trump in 2024.
      
    
              For now, Kamala's trading campaign stops for Chanel shops ... and keeping her options open for 2028.

              Hayden Panettiere left behind an estate worth at least $6 million, according to legal documents obtained by TMZ.
      
    
              Wladimir Klitschko -- the father of Hayden's daughter, Kaya -- filed documents petitioning the court to make a woman named Melissa Moskal Bencivenga the administrator of the estate. Melissa is a tax and financial advisor.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              The documents state Hayden died without a will and had personal property worth around $5.2 million and real property valued at just over $1 million. The total estate is said to be worth $6,232,119.
      

              We broke the story ... Hayden died of an accidental overdose in South Carolina back in August.
      
    
              Shortly after she died, Wladimir shared a tribute to Hayden ... saying she was loved, missed and will never be forgotten.
      
    
              Hayden was just 36 years old when she died.

title: Taylor Swift's Former Music Teacher Speaks Out After Vanity Fair Comments
description:
Taylor Swift's Ex Music Teacher
                          My Vanity Fair Interview Was Positive .
body:
Taylor Swift's Ex Music Teacher
                          My Vanity Fair Interview Was Positive ...
                          They Took It Out of Context
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Taylor Swift's former music teacher, who spoke about the singer to Vanity Fair, says she thinks highly of Taylor … despite what the article shared. 
      
    
              Sharon Luyben, who taught at Wyomissing Area Junior/Senior High for three decades, tells TMZ ... "All I said were positive things." 
      
    
              She tells us Taylor was a "fabulous student" and adds, "I was also a neighbor and friend with her parents who were very nice and active in our community."
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Vanity Fair did not use quotes from Sharon speaking highly of Taylor … instead, it used only one quote from her denying Taylor's claim that people didn't want to sit with her at lunch … and would move away from her. 
      
    
              Sharon told the reporter students had assigned seating at lunch … and, as such, Taylor's claim didn't make sense. Another student backed up the claim … while a second student the outlet spoke to wasn't sure. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The music teacher isn't the only one clearing the air after the article..
      
    
              Taylor's former classmate, Arielle Peppers, told us she wasn't trying to throw shade when she recalled a story about Taylor's expensive Ugg boots.
      
    
              As you know, Vanity Fair dropped a scathing profile of Taylor on Monday ... taking aim at her carefully cultivated image, personal relationships, and alleged industry feuds ... though she's reportedly not letting it get to her.

title: Bruce Willis' Gun From 'Die Hard' Up For Auction
description:
Bruce Willis
                          Welcome to the Auction, Pal ...
body:
Bruce Willis
                          Welcome to the Auction, Pal ...
                          John McClane's Sidearm On Sale!!!
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Bruce Willis fans ready to take back Nakatomi Tower -- or at least pretend they are -- can now buy an authentic weapon to fuel their daydreams ... because one of the prop guns the actor used in the OG "Die Hard" is set to be auctioned off.
      
    
              The Beretta 92F -- from Stembridge Gun Rentals -- is set to be sold by the Rock Island Auction Company as part of its Premier Auction in Bedford, Texas, from December 4-6.
      
    
              The gun itself will be sold December 5 ... and is expected to fetch between $75,000 and $150,000.
      

              The Beretta was one of two used in the film back in the day ... and Willis' character had it on him when Hans Gruber's crew took over the tower ... because he was a New York City cop who toted it with him all the way to L.A.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              BTW ... this Texas-based auction is full of famous firearms -- from weapons used in westerns like "Bonanza" and "El Dorado" to guns owned by big-time stars such as Frank Sinatra and Elvis Presley.
      
    
              "Die Hard" is a fan-favorite Christmas movie ... so we bet this Beretta would make a fantastic holiday gift ... if you've got some pretty deep pockets.
